test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 English Previous Paper 2 (Held On: 3 Feb 2022)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate indirect form of the given sentence.

“Good gracious! It’s snowing!” he said.

options.text: He remarked that it is snowing.
He happily said that it is snowing.
He said that good gracious it’s snowing.
He exclaimed with astonishment that it was snowing.

solution:
The correct answer is 'He exclaimed with astonishment that it was snowing.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

The given sentence is the exclamatory sentence that expresses wonder or astonishment.

We need to follow some basic rules to convert such types of sentences into indirect forms.

__
 
• 1. 'Said or said to' is changed as per the sense contained in the sentence.

 
 
• *Hurrah - exclaimed with joy.*
 
• *Alas - exclaimed with sorrow.*
 
• *Good gracious - exclaimed with wonder or astonishment.*
 
 
 
• 2. inverted commas (,") converted into **that.**
 
• **3. Interjections like hurrah, alas, or good gracious will be removed** and the rest of the sentence is changed per the simple sentence rule.

As per the above-given instructions, the given sentence should be - *'He exclaimed with astonishment that it was snowing.'*

Hence, the correct answer is **option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Let's understand the concept with some more examples.

 
• He said, "Good Gracious! What a huge snake."
 
 
• *He exclaimed with astonishment that it was a huge snake.*
 
 
 
• He said to me, "Alas! I could not save you".
 
 
• *He exclaimed with sorrow that he could not save me.*
